title: Epoch consistency gap during cross-region canary swap caused variant QPS surge and rollback pin deadlock
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: During a scheduled cross-region canary swap for model v2026-02-21, a mismatch in epoch propagation between the rollout coordinator and a subset of edge proxies produced an asymmetric traffic distribution that amplified QPS on the new variant by ~5x in eu-west-1 for ~3 minutes. The surge exhausted dedicated pool capacity for that variant, triggering autoscaler activity which was blocked by a version-pin that prevented timely scale-up. The combination caused increased latencies and ~12% of requests to time out for affected customers. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations performed during the incident, and the concrete follow-ups required to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-28T03:05Z - Deployment window: rollout coordinator initiated canary swap: global target weights 90% baseline / 10% canary
2026-02-28T03:06Z - Control-plane published epoch 8421; rollout coordinator marked canary active
2026-02-28T03:06:15Z - Edge proxies in eu-west-1 A/B subset received route table update with epoch 8421
2026-02-28T03:06:40Z - A small population (~7%) of edge proxies still operating on epoch 8420 due to intermittent fanout lag in the config distributor

2026-02-28T03:07:00Z - Because of a header-canonicalization difference between old/new route-translator logic, some requests were double-counted in the weight math causing the canary variant to receive >100% of expected canary traffic on those proxies
2026-02-28T03:07:30Z - Observability alerted: per-variant QPS spike in eu-west-1 canary shard (dashboard: RUNTIME/rollouts/variant-qps)
2026-02-28T03:08:00Z - Autoscaler detected sustained QPS increase and started scale-up decision tree
2026-02-28T03:08:30Z - Rollout coordinator attempted to rollback; a pre-existing version-pin on the canary shard prevented immediate instance replacement leading to scale-up backpressure
2026-02-28T03:09:30Z - Latency SLOs breached; on-call triggered incident bridge
2026-02-28T03:11:20Z - Emergency mitigation: control-plane forced an epoch fence and flushed route cache on all edges in eu-west-1 to re-homogenize routing state
2026-02-28T03:14:00Z - QPS and latency returned to near-normal; autoscaler converged and additional replicas came up after pin was cleared
2026-02-28T03:30:00Z - Incident declared resolved; post-incident monitoring continued for 24h
root_cause: A race between the config distributor fanout (some proxies applied epoch 8421 later than others) and a non-idempotent change in the route-translator header normalization logic introduced during the canary, causing weight accounting to be inconsistent across proxies. This produced local hotspots where the canary variant absorbed more requests than intended. The autoscaler could not immediately remediate because a previously applied version-pin (from an automated rollback protection step) prevented rapid replica admission, creating a deadlock between rollback/scale-up paths.
impact: Customer-facing: increased tail latency and ~12% timed-out requests for affected customers in eu-west-1 for ~3 minutes. Operational: brief exhaustion of dedicated canary pool, manual intervention required, PagerDuty incident and SEV-2 escalation.
mitigation_performed: Forced epoch fence and full route cache invalidation in eu-west-1 to align all edge proxies to epoch 8421
Cleared the stale version-pin on the canary shard to allow autoscaler to provision new replicas
Scoped canary to single AZ during emergency to limit blast radius while control-plane fixes propagated
Applied a temporary change to the route-translator to normalize headers consistently across epochs
action_items: (A1) Implement atomic epoch publish: switch config distributor to two-phase commit for route table updates to guarantee all edges move epochs in a single logical step — owner: Daniel Cho — due: 2026-03-26
(A2) Add preflight dry-run that compares old/new route-translator header normalization output against a golden corpus to catch non-idempotent changes — owner: Sofia Rivera — due: 2026-03-19
(A3) Add an autoscaler safety override: if rollback in progress, allow emergency ad-hoc scale-up for pinned shards to avoid deadlock — owner: Liam Barker — due: 2026-03-22
(A4) Instrument and add alert: per-variant QPS ratio vs expected weight > 1.5 for >30s in any region — owner: Priya Patel — due: 2026-03-05
(A5) Postmortem e2e test: simulate 50/50 split of proxies applying epochs with randomized propagation delays to validate rollout protocol — owner: Test Infra — due: 2026-04-02
(A6) Remove long-lived automatic version-pins; change to short TTLs with explicit approval workflow for long pins — owner: Security & Platform Policy — due: 2026-03-30
notes: This incident exposed two orthogonal weaknesses: (1) lack of atomicity in epoch propagation, and (2) complex interactions between rollback protection (version-pins) and autoscaler safety assumptions.
Config distributor telemetry did not expose the small fanout lag; adding per-edge apply-latency histograms recommended.
Edge proxies should treat route updates idempotently; any change that alters header normalization must be backwards compatible or gated behind an explicit migration path.
